name: Fx_ApplyAllParticleStates
signature: void Fx_ApplyAllParticleStates(FxParticle* particle)
summary: Applies both particle render-state groups: calls Fx_ApplyParticleState once with mode 0 and once with mode 1, so the particle's two packed state words are refreshed together.
evidence: The callee Fx_ApplyParticleState is now confident (0.50) and documented as 'applies one group of particle render flags'; this wrapper is exactly two calls with modes 0 and 1, i.e. both groups. The old name 'SetParticleFlags' described it as writing a flag word, which the body never does.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleTransform
signature: void maybe_Fx_SetParticleTransform(FxParticle** particle, u32* values)
summary: Copies a caller-supplied 3-float vector into the particle's render-transform block: values[2] to +0x60, values[1] to +0x64, values[0] to +0x68 (the engine stores the triple in reverse component order), then notifies the batch (0x52E3C8) and advances the emitter frame.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00527758: ldm r2,{r2,r3,ip}; ldr r1,[r1]; str ip,[r1,#0x60]!; str r3,[r1,#4]; str r2,[r1,#8] - a plain 3-word store, no matrix. The sibling 0x00528780 writes the same three floats from self+0x3C..0x44 into the shared render record, so the triple is a vector, but nothing names which vector; all four callers are maybe_ UpdateParticleList* walkers.

name: maybe_Fx_ResetParticleTransform
signature: void maybe_Fx_ResetParticleTransform(FxParticle** particle)
summary: Clears only the particle's +0x6C word (the fourth word of the render-transform block) and notifies the batch; it does not touch the three floats at +0x60/+0x64/+0x68, so 'Reset' means 'drop the marker', not 'zero the transform'.
evidence: Body is a single store of 0 to *particle+0x6C plus the batch notify and Fx_AdvanceEmitterFrame; the same word is cleared by 0x00528750 and left untouched by 0x00527758, so it is a marker word, but no caller or vtable sibling says what it marks.

name: maybe_Fx_SetParticleRotation
signature: void maybe_Fx_SetParticleRotation(FxParticle** particle, u32* values)
summary: Same three-float store as 0x00527758 (values[0] to +0x68, values[1] to +0x64, values[2] to +0x60) plus an explicit clear of the +0x6C marker word, then the batch notify and frame advance.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00528750 is 0x00527758 plus 'mov r2,#0; str r2,[r1,#0xc]' - identical stores, one extra clear. That makes the 'Rotation' half of the name unverifiable: the two functions write the same vector and differ only in the marker word.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListL
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListL(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Walks the particle's active sub-particle list (head at particle+0xE0, next at +0x14C): live entries get the per-particle update plus a vtable call, dead ones are unlinked with Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists, and the processed count lands in particle+0x284 before Fx_CommitParticleStream.
evidence: Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists is now confident (0.50) and is called by every member of this family at exactly the 'entry is dead' branch; the walk shape (f_E0 head, f_14C next, f_284 counter) is identical across L/M/N/O/Q/T, so only the letter disambiguates the per-particle helper each one uses.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListM
signature: void Fx_UpdateParticleListM(FxEmitter* self, FxParticle* particle)
summary: Short active-list updater: walks particle+0xE0 applying maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleB to live entries and unlinking dead ones, but when the emitter flag 0x400 is set it walks the alternate list at particle+0xE8 (next at +0x148) instead.
evidence: Same walker shape as its five siblings (f_E0/f_14C, f_284 counter) with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) on the dead branch; the 0x400 flag selects the second list head at +0xE8, which is the only structural difference from L.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListN
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListN(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Active-list updater that pairs maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleC (dead entries) with 0x526B98 plus the vtable call (live entries), counts them in particle+0x284 and commits the stream through maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream.
evidence: Identical control flow to Fx_UpdateParticleListL with a different per-particle helper pair; the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) and maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream appear at the same two points, which fixes the 'walk and update the active list' role.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListO
signature: void Fx_UpdateParticleListO(FxEmitter* self, FxParticle* particle)
summary: Minimal active-list updater: walks particle+0xE0 calling maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleC for each live entry, unlinks dead entries with Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists and counts the processed entries in particle+0x284.
evidence: The smallest member of the family (24 lines) and the clearest: one list head, one per-particle helper, the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) on the dead branch and the shared f_284 counter.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListQ
signature: u32 Fx_UpdateParticleListQ(FxEmitter* self, u32 arg2, FxParticle* particle, int forwarded, u32 arg5)
summary: Full active-list updater: resets the list through 0x527738, walks particle+0xE0 with maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleH plus the vtable call for live entries and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleD for dead ones, re-applies maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListP per entry and commits the stream.
evidence: Same walker skeleton as L/M/N/O/T (f_E0 head, f_14C next, f_284 counter) with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50) and maybe_Fx_CommitParticleStream at the same points; it is the richest variant, not a dispatcher - the four 'sibling' calls are the per-entry helpers, not a type switch.

name: Fx_UpdateParticleListT
signature: void Fx_UpdateParticleListT(FxEmitter* self, FxParticle* particle)
summary: Active-list updater that applies maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleD and maybe_Fx_UpdateParticleListP to every live entry and, for dead ones, advances the owning emitter's frame counter (f_154) before unlinking; the 0x400 emitter flag selects the alternate list at +0xE8.
evidence: Same walker skeleton as its five siblings with the now-confident Fx_UnlinkParticleFromLists (0.50); the extra block on the dead branch copies the emitter's f_5C..f_74 words into the render node, which is the same copy Fx_UpdateParticleListR/U perform.

name: Fx_AllocParticleNode
signature: u32* Fx_AllocParticleNode(FxParticlePool* self, FxParticleType* type, u32 flags)
summary: Hands out one 0x5880-byte block from the fixed pool at self+0x33C using the round-robin cursor self+0x444 masked by self+0x45C, links it into the per-type list at self+type*4+0x340 through the free-list word at +0x5870, stamps the flags/type words and returns it; returns 0 after self+0x450 failed probes.
evidence: The only real caller is the confident Fx_BuildParticleRenderQuad (0.50), which fixes the 'allocate a render block for the quad builder' role; the block is 0x5880 bytes with its list link at +0x5870, so 'node' means a pool node, not a single particle.

name: Gfx_LoadTextureByName
signature: int Gfx_LoadTextureByName(GfxResourceLoader* self, u32 out, const char* name)
summary: Asks the resource loader (virtual +0xC) for the named resource of type 'timg' (0x74696D67, the CTR texture container magic) and parses the returned block as a FLIM image through Gfx_Flim_Parse; returns 1 on success, 0 when the load or the parse fails.
evidence: The loader argument is the literal 0x74696D67 = 'timg', the CTR texture container magic, and the confident callee Gfx_Flim_Parse (0.50) parses exactly that format - together they pin 'texture', which the previous pass could only infer from the parse.

name: Ui_AnimClip_InitRuntime
signature: void Ui_AnimClip_InitRuntime(UiAnimClip* self)
summary: Shared runtime initialiser of a UI animation clip: clears the track count and the first/last list pointers, runs the one-time static-init guard for the keyframe container type, constructs the 0x48-byte keyframe buffer and clears the playback position.
evidence: Ui_AnimClip_CtorEmpty (0.50, vtable 0x00781348) calls it as its base initialiser, and the other eight callers are all UI sprite/animation creation sites (Ui_LayoutPane_InitFromRes, Battle_Popup_CreateChildSprite, Ui_HitIcon_CreateSprites, Ui_GuideWindow_AttachPlate), which fixes the class as the UI animation clip.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor_781498
signature: void maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor_781498(u32* self)
summary: Destructor for the UI widget class with vtable 0x00781498: destroys the child pointer array at +0xD0 (each child through its virtual destructor unless flagged), the single child at +0xD4, releases the buffer pair at +0xC4 and then runs the shared Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren base teardown.
evidence: The named callees Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren (0.55) and Mem_DeleteObject (0.55) plus Mem_FreeBufferPair (0x541B0C) fix the family as a UI widget destructor, but nothing ties vtable 0x00781498 to an 'AnimPlayer' class - that part came only from the N_069 proposal, so it is dropped.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor_7814F4
signature: void maybe_Ui_Widget_Dtor_7814F4(u32* self)
summary: Smaller sibling of 0x0053E8DC: installs vtable 0x007814F4, destroys the single child at +0xA4 through its virtual destructor, releases the buffer pair at +0xB8 and runs Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren.
evidence: Same body as 0x0053E8DC with one child instead of an array, and the same named callees (Ui_Widget_DestroyChildren 0.55, Mem_DeleteObject 0.55, Mem_FreeBufferPair); the 'AnimPlayer' class label is inherited from N_069 and only tied to the vtable constant, so it is dropped.

name: Fs_ArchiveStream_Seek
signature: int Fs_ArchiveStream_Seek(ArchiveStream* self, int offset)
summary: Performs one seek on an archive stream: forwards the caller's offset untouched in r1 to the archive helper 0x504FEC together with the stream's cached block handle, stores the returned position at request+0x18 and, when the operation reports completion, invokes the stream's completion callback (f_48) with the stored value.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00548218: r1 (the second argument) is never touched before 'bl 0x504FEC', so it is forwarded as the seek offset - the FACTS.md 'r1 forwarded untouched' trap. The only caller Sound_ArchiveStream_Open passes -0x10/-8/+8 for its three modes and its own doc already describes 0x548218 as the seek step.

name: maybe_Sound_Driver_StopTimer
signature: void maybe_Sound_Driver_StopTimer(SoundDriver* driver)
summary: One-shot shutdown step: when the driver's +0x1F4 flag is set it raises +0x1F7, calls the sound-system accessor 0x517A60 (whose return Ghidra drops) and clears +0x1F4.
evidence: The caller is the confident Sound_System_Shutdown (0.50), so the shutdown role is solid, but the callee 0x517A60 is only a three-instruction thunk onto Sound_GetSystem and its result is discarded, so nothing in the body says 'timer'; the +0x1F4/+0x1F7 flag pair is the only certain part.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat10
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat10(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0x10 of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x20 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask together with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: The callee Event_BroadcastSlotMask is now confident (0.50) and documented as 'loads the handler at self+0x90+i*4 for every set mask bit and calls it with the value in s0', which is exactly this wrapper's shape; the six siblings differ only in the table slot they load.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat0C
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat0C(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0xC of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x18 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: Same wrapper shape as its five siblings with table slot 3 (0x18); the now-confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50) is the only callee, and the two named callers Sound_Command_ExecuteList and Sound_Seq_ReadVarLenArg are sequencer command paths, which fits a channel-parameter setter.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat08
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat08(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0x8 of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x10 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: Same wrapper shape as its five siblings with table slot 2 (0x10); the now-confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50) is the only callee and the caller Sound_Command_ExecuteList is the sequencer command executor.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat104
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat104(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0x104 of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x30 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: Same wrapper shape as its five siblings with table slot 6 (0x30); the now-confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50) is the only callee, so the 'set one channel field on the masked channels' reading is fixed even though this variant has no direct caller.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat18
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat18(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0x18 of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x40 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: Same wrapper shape as its five siblings with table slot 8 (0x40); the now-confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50) is the only callee and the caller Sound_Command_ExecuteList is the sequencer command executor.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat14
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetChannelFloat14(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 channelMask, float value)
summary: Broadcasts one float to field +0x14 of every masked channel: loads the member-function pointer pair for that field from the channel-class table at 0x73D2E8+0x28 and hands it to Event_BroadcastSlotMask with the player's 16-slot channel array.
evidence: Same wrapper shape as its five siblings with table slot 5 (0x28); the now-confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50) is the only callee, so the 'set one channel field on the masked channels' reading is fixed even though this variant has no direct caller.

name: Sound_SeqPlayer_SetAllChannelNotesFlag
signature: void Sound_SeqPlayer_SetAllChannelNotesFlag(SoundSeqPlayer* player, u32 value)
summary: Stores the byte at player+0xE and then applies it to every note of all 16 channels: for each non-null entry of the channel array at player+0x90 it calls 0x54E2B0, which walks that channel's note list at +0x130 and flips the per-note flag +0x138.
evidence: The 16-slot channel array at player+0x90 is confirmed by the confident Event_BroadcastSlotMask (0.50), and the callee 0x54E2B0's body walks +0x130 nodes with the +0x138/+0x139 flag pair; its current name Font_GlyphList_SetVisible is a misnomer (it is also called from Sound_Command_ExecuteList), so the note-list reading comes from the body, not the name.

name: Ui_LayoutText_BuildGradientRamp
signature: void Ui_LayoutText_BuildGradientRamp(u32* out, u32 ctx, u32 start, u32 end)
summary: Builds the three-word gradient descriptor used by the text shading setup: compares the integer parts of two 8.24 fixed-point endpoints, clamps the extreme one, computes 0xFF00/(delta+1) and picks a shift (2/3/4) so the step fits in 8 bits, writing {end, start, shift|0x40} to out[0..2].
evidence: The only caller is the confident Ui_LayoutText_SetupMaterialAndShading (0.80), which passes a 3-word stack local; the body never touches a command buffer, so the old 'Gfx_CmdBuf' prefix was wrong. The 0x40 bit in out[2] is the 'ramp descends' flag, set when the start endpoint is above the end endpoint.

name: Text_CharFilter_Match
signature: u32 Text_CharFilter_Match(int self, u8* outVisible, int charRecord, int kind, u32 filter, int inRect, int x, int y, int minX, int maxX, int minY, int maxY, u32 layerMask)
summary: Decides whether one glyph is drawn: compares the glyph's layer/type bits (byte +2 & 0x1F, >>5) with the requested filter, tests the glyph rectangle against the clip rectangle and the 1<<(layer-1) layer mask, and returns 1 (draw) or 0 (skip) while also writing the decision to outVisible.
evidence: The caller Text_BuildGlyphQuads (0.50) and the 0x1F bit-field / 1<<(layer-1) convention are visible in the body; the previous doc claimed it 'always returns 1', but the body has eight 'return 0' branches, so it is a real predicate and the name holds.

name: Gfx_ModelSlot_Assign
signature: void Gfx_ModelSlot_Assign(void* self, void* resource, int slot, u32 context)
summary: Assigns a model-resource slot: if the slot table at (*(self+4))+0xC already holds an entry it is released through 0x52F6D0, and when a new resource is supplied its handle (resource+4) is installed with Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace using the owner at self+8.
evidence: Both callees are now named and both list this function as their only caller: maybe_Gfx_ModelSlot_Release (0.48) and Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace (0.50), whose docs already say 'the caller is Gfx_BindResourceSlot, so this is model-resource bookkeeping'. That fixes the subsystem the previous pass could only guess.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseSlotEmittersIfUnused
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseSlotEmittersIfUnused(Gfx_ModelInstance* self, InstanceSlot* slot)
summary: Drops the emitter group held by one instance slot: when the slot still points at the current resource (slot+8 == resource+0xC) and the resource is either still referenced (0x659318) or flagged (+0x288 / +4), it destroys the group with Fx_Group_DestroyEmitters and clears slot+4.
evidence: The teardown callee is the confident Fx_Group_DestroyEmitters (0.60), not a draw-node release, so the old 'ReleaseDrawNodes' wording was wrong; the two callers (Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses, Gfx_ModelInstance_SetMatrix) are draw-path functions, so when the condition actually fires is still unclear.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseBuffers
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_ReleaseBuffers(GfxModelInstance* self)
summary: Releases the two auxiliary buffers of a large Gfx object: frees +0x79C through 0x10F6CC and +0x7A0 through 0x10F69C (both are the 'load vtable from p-8, tail-call slot +4' deleting-destructor dispatch) and clears both fields.
evidence: Disassembly 0x00564054: ldr r0,[r0,#0x79c]; bl 0x10F6CC; str r5,[r4,#0x79c]; ldr r0,[r4,#0x7a0]; bl 0x10F69C; str r5,[r4,#0x7a0]. Both callees are the same 8-byte-header deleting-destructor thunk, so the release role is certain; the class is not, because the callers are Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release plus two overlay draw functions.

name: maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordPairB
signature: void maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordPairB(void** block)
summary: Releases the two owned pointers of a resource record - block[0] and block[7] (offset +0x1C) - through the deleting-destructor thunk 0x10F69C and clears both fields.
evidence: Eleven callers spread over Gfx, Ui, Pack and Anim (Gfx_Material_ResolveTextures, Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry, Anim_UpdateBlendTracks, Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateBlendSlots, Ui_SmithMenu_UpdatePageLabel), so this is a shared record-release helper, not a model function; the callee 0x10F69C is 'ldrd r0,r1,[p-8]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; bx r2', i.e. a deleting-destructor dispatch.

name: maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordTriple
signature: void maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordTriple(void** self)
summary: Releases the three owned pointers of a resource record - self[0], self[3] (+0xC) and self[7] (+0x1C) - and zeroes the six header words self[0..5]; same body as 0x00579794 plus the third pointer.
evidence: Same body as 0x00579794 (template copy) with one extra 'if (self[7]) free' block; the only caller is Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release, and the callee 0x10F69C is the deleting-destructor thunk, so the release role is certain and the record layout is exact, but the record's meaning is not.

name: maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordPair
signature: void* maybe_Mem_ReleaseRecordPair(void** self)
summary: Releases the two owned pointers of a resource record - self[0] and self[3] (+0xC) - and zeroes the six header words self[0..5]; returns the record pointer.
evidence: Same body as 0x00569CB8 minus the third free (template copy); the callee 0x10F69C is the deleting-destructor thunk ('ldrd r0,r1,[p-8]; ldr r2,[r0]; ldr r2,[r2,#4]; bx r2'), so this is a record release helper, not a model-specific one.

name: maybe_Model_ReleasePartBuffers
signature: void maybe_Model_ReleasePartBuffers(ModelInstance* self)
summary: Releases the per-part buffers of a large model object: frees the three pointers at self+0x298 (stride 4) and the two 3-word blocks at +0xE88 and +0xEA4, clearing every field it frees.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Gfx_CharShadowPass_Release (0.50), which fixes the teardown role; the five free calls all go to the deleting-destructor thunk 0x10F69C, but the object identity (model instance vs shadow-pass state) is still only an offset reading.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverridePass
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverridePass(Gfx_ModelInstance* self, u32 cmdList, u32 arg3)
summary: Draws an instance through its material-override list when it has one (self->f_20->f_154): runs the override-material pass and, if that pass did not consume the override (the 5/0x11 pair is unchanged), submits the packed skinning data directly.
evidence: Both callees are now confident - Gfx_ModelInstance_SubmitSkinningData (0.50) and maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawOverrideMaterialPass - and the caller Gfx_Overlay_DrawMainScreen (0.50) is the overlay draw path, which is where an override pass belongs.

name: Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPart
signature: void Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPart(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Emits the texture-unit command chain for one textured part and draws it: Gfx_Pica_EmitDrawElements, Gfx_Pica_EmitTextureSamplerStateEx, Gfx_CommandNode_BuildChain4, Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureDescriptor, Gfx_GpuCmd_WriteTextureUnitBlock, then Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureAndDraw.
evidence: The readable body is damaged by Ghidra's coprocessor modelling, but the disassembly at 0x00568F84 is a clean sequence of six named Gfx calls ending in Gfx_ModelInstance_BindTextureAndDraw (0x568BB4); nothing in it touches a texture matrix, so the old 'ApplyTextureMatrixA' name was wrong.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPartB
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_DrawTexturedPartB(int self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int arg4)
summary: Second texture-unit emitter of the model-instance draw code: loops over the part's texture units calling 0x656ACC/0x65654C/0x658050 and Gfx_CommandNode_InitSixSlots, then binds and draws; the symbol size (132 bytes) is wrong, the body runs past 0x569368.
evidence: Disassembly 0x005692CC onward calls the same texture-unit helpers as 0x00568F84 (0x656ACC, 0x65654C, 0x658050, 0x50971C) and loops on a state word compared with 2; the 'ApplyTextureMatrixB' name is not supported by any of those calls, but the exact draw role of this variant is still unclear.

name: maybe_Font_GlyphCache_FindSlotA
signature: u32 maybe_Font_GlyphCache_FindSlotA(FontCache* self, void* out, u32 key)
summary: Looks up one glyph slot in the cache table at self+0x2C: when the key carries the 0x2000000 flag and the low 16 bits resolve through 0x7141EC, it touches the slot through 0x1235A4 and returns 1, otherwise 0.
evidence: The only caller is the confident Font_CacheGlyphsForText (0.60), whose doc lists 0x00589Dxx among the glyph-upload helpers, so the 'Gfx_Scene_CollectNodeType' name was wrong; the two tables (self+0x2C here, self+4 in 0x00589D94) and the 0x2000000/0x1000000 flag split are still unexplained.

name: maybe_Font_GlyphCache_FindSlotB
signature: u32 maybe_Font_GlyphCache_FindSlotB(FontCache* self, void* out, u32 key)
summary: Same lookup as 0x00589D54 against the second cache table at self+4: when the key carries the 0x1000000 flag and the low 16 bits resolve through 0x71423C, it touches the slot through 0x1235A4 and returns 1, otherwise 0.
evidence: Same body as 0x00589D54 with the other table (self+4) and the other flag bit (0x1000000); the caller Font_CacheGlyphsForText (0.60) is the same, so the glyph-cache attribution holds while the meaning of the two tables does not.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_SetupAttachments
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_SetupAttachments(MemberScreen* screen)
summary: Sub-update of the battle member screen: links the member actors, then for every hidden member (slot +0x4C, flag +0x10 == 0) calls the effect object's virtual +0x98, and for every visible member (slot +0x48) sets its state to 4 through virtual +0x3C and releases the attachment at +0x224.
evidence: The caller Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_Update (0.50) fixes the class, and the two loops are clearly 'hidden members' vs 'visible members' (the +0x10 flag is tested both ways); 'SetupAttachments' is still a reading of the virtual +0x98/+0x3C calls.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_RefreshChildPositions
signature: void maybe_Battle2DUnit_RefreshChildPositions(Battle2DUnit* self)
summary: Refreshes the unit's derived screen geometry: calls the unit's virtual transform refresh (+0x3C) and child-slot reset (+0x54, index 0), then, when the unit has more than one child (0x630D64), recomputes the adjusted screen position with Battle2DUnit_GetAdjustedScreenPosition.
evidence: The callee Battle2DUnit_GetAdjustedScreenPosition is now confident (0.50) and the caller Battle2DUnit_CalcMoveDuration (0.50) is the repositioning path, which fits; the child-count gate (0x630D64 > 1) is the only support for the 'child' wording.

name: Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateWithScaleOverride
signature: void Gfx_RenderObject_UpdateWithScaleOverride(RenderObject* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Render-object update variant: when the parameter object (self+0x208) is flagged at +0x1A it writes that object's +0xC value into the renderer's scale field at (*(*(self+0x10+4)+0x160))+0x134, runs the prepare hook and the renderer's virtual +0x9C, then tail-calls Gfx_RenderObject_Update.
evidence: The tail callee Gfx_RenderObject_Update is now confident (0.50) and the body stores exactly one float into the renderer's scale field - the same field 0x005A9D58 multiplies by f_20C - so 'WithScaleOverride' is supported and the earlier 'WithMatrix' wording named the wrong parameter.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite_InitSharedContext
signature: void maybe_Gfx_Sprite_InitSharedContext(int* desc)
summary: Lazily creates the shared sprite render context singleton at 0x007BE318 (0x60-byte objects, vtable 0x007829A4, built by Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init) and, when the descriptor has a UV/index pair at +8, pushes it through 0x2E7798.
evidence: The singleton creation is the same one 0x005AA038 performs and the callee Gfx_Scene_SpriteCtx_Init (0.50) is named, but the function has no caller and the second half is a single UV call, so 'InitSharedContext' still overstates the role.

name: Field2D_MapChip_ScanColumnToEdge
signature: void Field2D_MapChip_ScanColumnToEdge(u32* outCell, u32 map, u32* cell, int count)
summary: Walks one column of the chip grid until the run of kind-2 chips ends: with count != 0 it steps +2 per iteration, otherwise -2, decoding each cell with Field2D_DecodeChipWallType, and writes the last cell that was still kind 2 to outCell.
evidence: Six named callers, all map-chip queries (Field2D_MapChip_TestCellWalkable, Field2D_MapChip_MapPointToCell, Field2D_MapChip_SelectEntry, Field2D_MapChip_ScanRegionTiles, Field2D_Actor_StepMoveTargets, Field2D_Scene_RenderObjectBatch), and the body accumulates nothing - it only advances by +-2 while the decoded kind stays 2, so 'GetColumnInfo' described a query that does not exist.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryA
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryA(u32* cells, u32 map, int step, char* kindOut)
summary: Four-byte Thumb entry that branches into the shared chip-column walker with its own starting offset; the walker steps cells[1] by -2 while the decoded chip kind stays 2 and writes the final cell through the caller's out pointer.
evidence: The address is a 4-byte branch stub and the body Ghidra attaches to it is the shared walker with unaff_r4/unaff_r6 registers (damaged decompilation, FACTS.md), so no direction can be recovered; 'WalkDirection' claimed one, 'WalkEntry' does not.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryB
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryB(u32* cells, u32 map, int step, char* kindOut)
summary: Second four-byte Thumb entry into the shared chip-column walker; differs from 0x005BFB2E only in the branch offset, and the shared body steps cells[1] by -2 while the decoded chip kind stays 2.
evidence: Same 4-byte stub pattern as 0x005BFB2E and the same shared body with unaff_r4/unaff_r6 registers (damaged decompilation, FACTS.md); nothing distinguishes a direction, so the name no longer claims one.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryC
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_WalkEntryC(u32* cells, u32 map, int step, char* kindOut)

name: maybe_Text_WindowQueue_Advance
signature: void maybe_Text_WindowQueue_Advance(TextQueueEntry* self, BattleTextWindow** window)
summary: Four-state step function for a queued battle-text request: state 0 waits four frames then pushes the message, state 1 waits for the panel animation and calls the stored commit callback, state 2 ensures the sub-panel and advances, state 3 hides it.
evidence: The callee Battle_TextWindow_EnsureSubPanel is now confident (0.50) and the state byte at +4 / frame counter at +8 are clear, but the four callers (Ui_HandleSet_IsReady, Field2D_Scene_StartConditionTask, Gfx_RenderState_Setup, Field2D_Map_StartLayerTask) look like generic task runners, so 'queue' is still an interpretation.

name: maybe_Field2D_Actor_BeginMoveTask
signature: unsigned maybe_Field2D_Actor_BeginMoveTask(void* taskMemory, Field2DActor* actor, unsigned target, const void** callbacks)
summary: Initialises a movement task on a field 2D actor: stores the local continuation address as the task entry, copies the three callback words and the target into the task header, installs the step callbacks at actor+0x2FC/+0x300/+0x304 and starts the interpolation (0x63B9A8/0x6683A4/0x667CB4).
evidence: The body ends in halt_baddata() and uses _LAB_ symbols for the continuation addresses, i.e. damaged decompilation (FACTS.md), so the confidence stays at 0.30; the caller Field2D_Scene_StartPathTask (0.50) does support the 'begin a move task' reading.

name: maybe_Text_SpanCursor_Init
signature: SpanCursor* maybe_Text_SpanCursor_Init(SpanCursor* self, TextContext* ctx, int mode)
summary: Initialises a span-cursor sub-object: installs vtable 0x00783BA0, stores the mode, computes the first offset from the context's +0x78 through 0x6685EC and clears the direction/flag/count fields.
evidence: The only caller Field2D_SpriteNode_UpdateAnimation (0.55) also drives the confident Text_SpanCursor_Next (0x5CDF3C) on the same sub-object at self+0xA8, so the class is shared between text and 2D sprite sequence playback and the 'text' prefix is not wrong - but the caller is a sprite node, so the role is still only 'init a cursor'.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ClearAllChildren
signature: void maybe_Field_Gimmick_ClearAllChildren(FieldGimmick* self)
summary: Clears every child element of a field gimmick: resets the UI mode pair, takes the child container from self+0x10, and for each of its +0x1460 entries clears the child's +0xA2 flag, calls its virtual +0x80 release and unregisters it.
evidence: The callee Field_Gimmick_SetUiModePair (0.50) fixes the class, and the loop over the container's +0x1460 entries with a vtable+0x80 release is a clear child teardown; the function has no caller, so 'children of a gimmick' is still an interpretation of the container field.
